title.value: A Reproducible and Realistic Evaluation of Partial Domain Adaptation Methods
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the beginning of the paper, indicating the focus on evaluating partial domain adaptation methods.
title.quote: A Reproducible and Realistic Evaluation of Partial Domain Adaptation Methods

extractions.description: The paper evaluates Partial Domain Adaptation (PDA) methods with a focus on model selection strategies that do not require target labels, as this is a common assumption in PDA scenarios. The authors conduct experiments on real-world datasets to provide a comprehensive evaluation of different PDA algorithms and model selection strategies.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper directly discusses methods related to domain adaptation in machine learning, with no specific focus on Climate Change or its related challenges. The themes deal more with the technical aspects of model evaluation in machine learning rather than Climate Change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) aims at classifying unlabeled target images leveraging source labeled ones.

primary_category.justification: The content does not address any Climate Change categories as it focuses on domain adaptation techniques in machine learning.
primary_category.quote: The main goal of this work is to provide a realistic evaluation of PDA methods with the different model selection strategies under a consistent evaluation protocol.

primary_sub_category.justification: Given that the paper does not align with any specific Climate Change sub-categories, focusing instead on domain adaptation in AI, no sub-category is relevant.
primary_sub_category.quote: We consider the Partial Domain Adaptation (PDA) variant, where we have extra source classes not present in the target domain.

new_primary_category.quote: In this work, we conduct extensive experiments to study the impact of model selection strategies on the performance of partial domain adaptation methods.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: Most successful algorithms use model selection strategies that rely on target labels to find the best hyper-parameters and/or models along training.
